The architecture is a **shared tax-automation core with provider namespaces behind a registry**. It is partly migrated: **Instead is the only registered adapter**. Juno still has legacy code and storage; GruntWorx is already an enum value, but that does not make it an available adapter.

**Vendor-neutral ports**

The shared namespace is `TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations`. Its main boundaries are:

| Area | Shared services and responsibilities |
|---|---|
| Connection lifecycle | `Authorizations::Create`, `Connections::{Create, Find, Disconnect, Renew, Revoke, VerifyGrant, DisconnectAll}` |
| Export | `ExportAsync` authorizes, validates capabilities, creates shared send records, then delegates delivery |
| Tax-preparation envelopes | `TaxPreparations::{FindOrCreate, BatchDestroy, DestroyForClient, DestroyForContact, MergeForContact}` |
| Form prefill | `TaxPreparationPrefills::Find` reads shared history and firm settings |
| Document lifecycle | Shared upload/status handling, status broadcasts, resumption, and presigned byte transfer |
| Firm lifecycle | Deactivation releases grants; destruction removes shared records and invokes adapter cleanup |

The core owns the user-facing vocabulary and validation. The adapter owns vendor API calls, delivery orchestration, vendor identifiers, and mapping vendor statuses into shared statuses. For example, callbacks and scheduled checks report normalized processing status through [`Documents::UpdateStatus`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/documents/update_status.rb:3).

The universal API is separately gated by `tax_automations_unified_api`; Instead availability is gated by `tax_automations_instead`. Both flags default to disabled in the feature configuration.

**How an adapter plugs in**

[`Registry`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/lib/tax_preparation/tax_automations/registry.rb:6) uses explicit registration:

```ruby
ADAPTERS = {instead: TaxPreparation::TaxAutomations::Instead}.freeze
FEATURE_FLAGS = {instead: :tax_automations_instead}.freeze
```

There is no automatic discovery. `FirmSettings.provider` selects the adapter for new work. Existing connection operations resolve the vendor from the connection’s namespace; send records retain their own provider snapshot.

Production dispatch sites require the following members under an adapter namespace:

| Member | Contract |
|---|---|
| `Connection` | ActiveRecord model supporting shared OAuth lifecycle, capability passport, firm lookup and background queries |
| `Client` | Constructible with a connection; shared lifecycle calls need `renew!` and `revoke_tokens!` |
| `Authorizations::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, return_url)` → authorization URL |
| `Connections::Create` | `.call(user, actor, provider, params)` → connection |
| `ExportAsync` | `.call(user, actor, tax_preparation, tax_automation_documents:)` |
| `Documents::ReconcileStatusesAsync` | `.call(user, actor, connection, {tax_automation_document_ids:})` |
| `DestroyForTaxPreparations` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, tax_preparations)` |
| `MergeForContact` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id, source_contact_id, target_contact_id)` |
| `DestroyForFirm` | `.call(user, actor, firm_id)` |

These are Ruby conventions enforced through dispatch, rather than a single formal adapter interface. Background reconciliation and firm cleanup therefore matter when defining a complete adapter.

The current connection contract is **OAuth-oriented**: `HasOauthConnection` supplies encrypted credentials and the states `disconnected`, `connected`, `expired`, and `revoked`. Both connected and expired grants are usable because refresh can recover an expired grant. Instead’s client extends `BaseClient`, inheriting `TokenRefreshable`, and declares OAuth endpoints and credentials through `.oauth2_settings`.

Provider switching happens when connection creation succeeds, inside the core transaction. Starting consent leaves the existing provider intact. The core also binds the firm to an external vendor account and rejects a reconnect into another account. See [`Connections::Create`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/connections/create.rb:43).

**The capability passport**

[`HasCapabilities`](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/has_capabilities.rb:17) defines a typed, class-level passport:

```text
Capabilities
  supported_tax_years: Integer[]
  terms:
    return_type: String
    accepted_file_formats: String[]
    max_file_size_mb: positive Integer
```

Capabilities describe the vendor, so reading them requires no connection row. Each adapter implements private class methods `capability_terms` and `supported_tax_years`; grouped terms expand into one entry per return type.

The passport validates extension spelling, positive size limits, duplicate return-type declarations, and years between 2000 and the current year plus one. Supported return types derive from the terms.

It serves two purposes:

- The shared export validator rejects unsupported forms, years, formats, and oversized files before dispatch.
- The API serializer exposes `tax_years` and `return_types`, enriching each form with its display name, personal/business family, `file_types`, and `file_size_limit`.

See the [validator](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/export/validate_documents.rb:40) and [serializer](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/serializers/tax_preparation/base/tax_automations/connection_serializer.rb:57).

Instead currently declares all 11 mapped core return types, the current year and previous two years, eight configured file extensions, and a configurable size limit defaulting to 2000 MB. Validation converts that limit using Rails `.megabytes`.

**The data model**

| Model | Purpose and identity |
|---|---|
| `FirmSettings` | One row per firm: selected provider and external tenant/account UUID. Provider enum: `juno: 0`, `gruntworx: 1`, `instead: 2` |
| Shared `TaxPreparation` | Tax-return envelope containing firm, client, optional contact, year, return type, EIN and business name |
| Shared `Document` | A send of one TaxDome document, scoped by **firm + envelope + document + provider + return type** |
| Instead `Connection` | One grant per firm, creator attribution, encrypted tokens and expiries, lifecycle timestamps, external UUID, PKCE ceremony fields |
| Instead `Entity` | Vendor taxpayer/entity handle, entity type, client/contact linkage, source and synchronization/archive information |
| Instead `Document` | One-to-one extension of a shared send, storing vendor file UUID, path, and Instead entity reference |

Two distinctions matter:

- The envelope still uses the physical **`juno_tax_preparations` table**. Its core lookup key is firm/client/contact/year; changing return type updates that envelope. Each send separately snapshots its return type and provider.
- The shared send owns two independent state machines: upload (`waiting`, `uploading`, `uploaded`, `failed`) and processing (`sent`, `processing`, `processed`, `error`, `archived`, `exceeded`), plus normalized failure reasons.

Sources: [envelope model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparation.rb:3), [envelope lookup](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/services/tax_preparation/tax_automations/tax_preparations/find_or_create.rb:98), and [send model](/Users/Shared/nav-ab/repo-master/app/models/tax_preparation/tax_automations/document.rb:7).

For GruntWorx, the existing extension boundary is clear, but its authentication and delivery model must fit these current OAuth and background-service contracts—or those shared contracts will need extending. No files were edited.
